title: The integral constructible category and its heart
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, let $\ell$ be a prime different from $p$, and let $X$ be a separated scheme of finite type over $k$, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Coefficients are the completed ring sheaf $R_X=\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$ of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and the ambient category is the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_X))$ of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Use the constructibility and bounded constructibility of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the standard truncations of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], and the fixed-universe size convention [def-weil-size-convention].

1. $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is a full triangulated subcategory of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_X))$ in the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Its objects are bounded, and it is stable under the standard truncations.
2. $\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$ identifies with the objects of $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ concentrated in degree $0$. It is an abelian full subcategory of $\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$: kernels and cokernels of its morphisms, computed in $\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$, belong to it. It is closed under extensions and essentially small (its isomorphism classes form a set in the chosen universe).

proof.text: The finite-type scheme is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, hence Noetherian. Replace the arbitrary-universe finite extension by its small Shrink. Apply [lem-int-integral-coefficient-ring-comparison] to embed it as a finite intermediate field in the fixed algebraic closure and identify the condensed integer ring.

Transport [lem-sfb-integral-constant-model-heart-closure] along this condensed ring isomorphism. Restriction of scalars along a ring isomorphism preserves finite presentations: it preserves the regular module, finite biproducts and presentation cokernels. Its natural compatibility with inverse image proves equivalence of finite constant local models on the same covers and strata. It preserves kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences, so the constructibility predicate for the original coefficient ring is closed under all three operations.

Finite presentations show zero and isomorphism closure directly. Apply the already proved generic homologyProperty_isTriangulated declaration recorded on [prop-constructible-derived-subcategory] to the weak Serre class constructed in step 2, then intersect with the bounded property. The proved homologyProperty_truncLE and homologyProperty_truncGE preserve the same cohomology predicate: each retained cohomology is the original one and each discarded cohomology is zero. The standard t-structure bounds show that both truncations remain bounded.

A constructible module placed in degree zero has bounded constructible cohomology. Conversely [lem-sf-derived-concentrated-single] identifies a degree-zero bounded constructible complex with its constructible zeroth cohomology. [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] identifies all morphisms as well. Extension closure and the split biproduct exact sequence give finite product closure. Mathlib CategoryTheory.Abelian.Subcategory gives abelianness from zero, kernel, cokernel and finite-product closure.

By [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model], a finite constant local model is locally finitely presented. Transport the stratum restrictions along the canonical coefficient isomorphisms using [lem-weil-pbc-module-constructible-pullback]. Thus constant-model constructible objects form a subproperty of the ambient constructible module-object property. Apply [lem-sfb-constructible-module-objects-essentially-small], and inherit essential smallness for the smaller full subcategory.

proof_origin.place: Assertions 1--2; reuse existing weak Serre closure and essential-smallness theorems, then the proved homology-property API; recovered C2 proof and repaired definitional-equality elaboration; G2 repair: local irreducibility of pullback definitions and abstract-coefficient assembly keep elaboration below the standard limits, without changing any data or public signature.

split_report.summary: Expanded the imported two-paragraph proof into nine steps using existing nodes only. Made the standing geometric and coefficient hypotheses explicit; used the actual integral-model equivalence rather than treating completeness as a definition. Cited finite-coefficient triangulation and étale origin separately. Verified the cone kernel/cokernel identifications and ambient extension triangle. Replaced unspecified global gluing data by an explicit adjunction-unit monomorphism and a sectionwise subobject count. No new nodes or Mathlib leaves. The final clause audit also cites concentration and single-complex full faithfulness to justify the heart identification on objects and morphisms. Second reading adds the explicit Noetherianity citation and counts overlap morphisms sectionwise; no new nodes. Landing-refusal repair (2026-10-17): re-read all 23 cited proof-node statements against the current DAG; refreshed the obsolete cartesian-coefficients quote; step 8 now explicitly uses its canonical underlying-sheaf natural isomorphism and applies stratum zero detection to the underlying abelian sheaf. No statement, route, new-node or hypothesis change. Independent second reading: wrote the stratum-unit map and its retraction using the chosen local-model isomorphism explicitly; all 34 quotations revalidated.
split_report.blueprint: Proof paragraph (1) realized by steps 1–4: completeness, exact reduction, finite constructibility, triangulation, boundedness and truncations. Paragraph (2) realized by steps 5–6 for the abelian heart and extensions, and steps 7–9 for the finite presentation/cover/gluing-data size argument. The chapter and unit route are preserved.

tool_uses.why: Finiteness of the residue field permits application of the finite-ring constructibility tools; this is a generic coefficient-field fact.
Cone and shift closure for derived completeness; the integral-heart unit invokes these as generic completion facts.
Exactness of derived reduction as a ringed-site scalar-extension functor; no heart-unit statement supplies that functorial exactness.
Triangulation for the finite residue-field complexes used in the unit residue-reduction route.
Bounded finite-coefficient intrinsic constructibility has étale origin; keeps the actual hypothesis of the integral-model criterion.
The ambient long exact sequence identifies the kernel and cokernel; a general derived-category tool.
An ambient short exact sequence of degree-zero complexes gives its distinguished triangle.
Exact module inverse images for the actual pulled-back integral coefficients, used only in the size argument.
Joint zero detection of finite stratum restrictions proves the global adjunction-unit map is monic; no integral-heart-unit statement supplies it.
The general concentration theorem identifies a complex with only H^0 with a degree-zero module; it makes essential surjectivity of the heart identification explicit.
Full faithfulness of the single-complex functor identifies the morphisms of the degree-zero subcategory with module morphisms.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q20-14671086d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 8 statement dependencies and all 23 proof dependencies in full, plus the blueprint's triangulated, unit and local-model proof texts and Stacks proetale.tex 09C1/09C2. The coefficient category is D(Mod(R_X)) with R_X = p_X^* O_E throughout; completeness, Nakayama and integral-models(2) are all stated for R_X, and the item never identifies R_X with the constant sheaf C_X. Step 1: integral-models(2) is an actual if-and-only-if, the residue field is finite, and X is Noetherian. Steps 2-3: shift and cone closure of derived completeness, exact reduction to kappa, the finite-ring triangulation lemma, and both directions of the étale-origin equivalence; the item rightly does not use the 09C2 boundedness shortcut, since 09C2 assumes finite tor dimension. Step 4: boundedness holds by the cohomological definition and the degree-zero identification is correct. Step 5: kernel and cokernel are H^{-1} and H^0 of the cone, checked on a zero map and an isomorphism. Step 6: the cone of zero gives direct sums, and short exact sequences give triangles. Steps 7-9: the uniqueness-of-gluing argument, the split adjunction unit and stratum zero detection with identity covers are correct, and the subobject count is valid. Edge cases checked: empty X, and multiplication by pi on O_{E,X}. There are no new nodes, no cycle (the item is not reachable from anything it cites) and no duplicate (det-lem-coefficient-heart-small covers only E and Qlbar; prop-constructible-truncations covers another category). I accept the 11 declared generic tool_uses. Caution for later, not a fault here: the blueprint proof of local-model(3) uses this item's clause 1, so whoever splits det-lem-int-integral-heart-local-model must prove (2) and (3) directly from the cohomological definition, not by citing this item. No fixes.

lean.note: The theorem uses the recorded finite constant scalar-model constructibility predicate, not the upstream arbitrary-presentation predicate. The real-data coefficient helper transports an arbitrary-universe finite extension through Shrink.algEquiv, using Module.Finite.small, and applies the existing continuous-function condensed ring construction to its spectral-norm valuation ring. No embedding in PadicAlgCl or equality of coefficient and scheme universes is required.
